text:
sam: Heads up — flipped a canary for tsuru-compact v0.4 (q5) on staging. Quick eval shows ja->en BLEU drift and some mirrored punctuation for he/ar.

nora: ow. numbers?

sam: ran the parallel suite (small dev shard):
```
./eval_runner --model tsuru-compact:v0.4-q5 --tasks ja->en,zh->en,he->en,ar->en --metrics bleu,bracket_flip,punct_mirror --out /tmp/tsuru-q5-173901
```
results top-level:
- ja->en BLEU: 29.0 (baseline 31.8)
- zh->en BLEU: 32.5 (baseline 32.9)
- he->en punctuation_mirror: 1.8% (baseline 0.2%)
- ar->en punctuation_mirror: 1.4% (baseline 0.15%)

jia: ja drop is annoying. is it tokenization or decode?

sam: dug a few failing pairs. Token boundary example (baseline vs q5):
```
baseline tokens: [][][]  <-- (actual tokens shown as ideographs for brevity)
baseline: [日][本][語][。]\nq5 tokens:     [日本語][。]
```
So q5 merges ideographs into a single subtok early and changes alignment when computing ngram matches.

olav: merging like that can change greedy path too. Was vocab altered?

sam: vocab hash matches the spec. However decoding top-k differs on first 10 tokens for JA samples.

mica: I saw similar in another run — the vertical layout tests (linewrap) also regress: long ruby/kanji sequences insert ZERO-WIDTH SPACE oddly and cause linebreaks mid-word in vertical render tests. Might be detokenizer trimming zwsp.

jia: can you paste a minimal repro for mirrored punctuation?

sam: here: input Hebrew snippet + output
```
input: "שלום (א, ב) סדר האיברים"\nbaseline decode: "elements (A, B) kept order"
q5 decode:     "elements )A, B( kept order"
```
mirrored parentheses swapped.

quant-bot: NOTE: q5 uses layerwise asymmetric per-channel quantization, rounding=nearest by default.

olav: that smells like detok/mirroring is sensitive to token adjacency — if tokens split differently we may flip the bidi algorithm post-hoc.

mica: action plan proposal:
1) enable shadow_fp32 echo on the staging model to capture logits (expensive).
2) run beam=4 to see if beam recovers baseline paths.
3) histogram tokenization diffs across dev shard and add locale-specific gate for ja BLEU drop > 1.0
4) add a short detok middleware that enforces bracket pairing for RTL locales as a short-term mitigation.

sam: agree. infra-bot — can we toggle shadow_fp32 and set rounding=stochastic for one canary?

infra-bot: @sam yes. Commands:
```
redwood deploy update --model tsuru-compact:v0.4-q5 --set shadow_fp32=true --set rounding=stochastic --note "ja/rtl-eval-debug"
```
Also you can pin KERNEL_PROFILE=testbed to force fallback kernels.

(some time passes)

sam: ran 1 & 2. Shadow vs baseline match: ja top-1 token match 97.0% overall but drops to 92.4% for long-kanji sequences (>6 ideographs). Beam-4 recovers baseline path on ~60% of those failing samples, so search helps but doesn't fully mask.

jia: interesting. any per-layer metrics?

sam: captured pre-softmax variance per-layer. Layers 5-7 show reduced dynamic range (~10% reduction in variance) only for long-kanji inputs on q5 path.

olav: that fits an accumulator saturation / scale mismatch in middle layers. Quant-team: any kernel changes in v0.4 Q5?

quant-bot: we pushed a reordered matmul kernel for speed on T4 in q5; it uses fused requantization with int32 accumulators truncated to int16 for memory. Known risk: small magnitude logits can clip. Opening ticket now.

mica: long-term fixes: change accumulator width or per-layer scaling; short-term: set rounding=stochastic and fallback to baseline kernels for JA and RTL locales in canary routing.

sam: created issue #3290 with logs, sample ids, and a small failing file of 120 samples. Tagging @quant and @infra. Priority P2.

infra-bot: Canary snapshot saved: canary-173901-tsuru-q5-debug

mia: (note) I can prototype a detok-middleware that, after token-level join, runs a small pass: if locale in [he,ar] and an adjacent token pair equals bracket-open + alpha then force mirror ordering on output. Lightweight and reversible.

jia: good. Also add a unit test that compares tokenization boundary counts between baseline and quantized models; fail the canary if >1% divergence for ja.

olav: I'll try repro on A100 int8 path this afternoon — if A100 doesn't reproduce we can route ja traffic to a100 until quant fix lands.

sam: thanks. I'll post updates. For now pausing rollout.

quant-bot: reminder: stochastic rounding may hide a systemic bias; prefer fixing accumulators upstream.

sam: agreed. I'll keep canary blocked until quant-team suggestions land. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
